text:
Arseny Gritsyuk, a 2019 sixth-round pick (129th overall) out of Omsk, scored twice for New Jersey, and the second goal was the kind that sinks a team. His backhand with under two minutes left in the second period came on a 3% chance by our numbers, and it made the score NJD 4, VGK 2. Jack Hughes added two of his own, the last an empty-looking third-period backhand that put the game away at 5-2.

The scoreboard was closer than the first period suggested. Vegas led 2-1 late in the first, after Mark Stone scored on the power play and Ivan Barbashev followed 1:30 later, and by expected goals (the quality of the chances each side created) VGK held the better of that period, 0.76 to 0.53. Then Gritsyuk tied it with 69 seconds left, and the night belonged to the Devils. They out-chanced Vegas 1.23 to 0.43 in the second and finished with 63 shot attempts to 39. The simulated replays of every shot give NJD a 61% chance to win this game, so the result was fair. Vegas did hit 36 times to New Jersey's 13 and blocked 15 shots, but it gave the puck away 15 times and took it away once.

Adin Hill allowed about 1.6 goals more than the shots he faced should have produced, while Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 of 21 and was fine rather than spectacular. The facts we have don't include either team's streak or record, so we'll only say that New Jersey leaves Las Vegas with a win built on its two Hughes brothers and its late-first-period answer, and Vegas leaves wondering how a 2-1 lead became a three-goal loss.
